title: Minister announces plans to strengthen power infrastructure across A.P.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Minister for Energy Gottipati Ravi Kumar said that the government was considering strengthening power infrastructure across the State to ensure uninterrupted supply, daytime power for agriculture, and expansion of renewable energy.

The Minister was reviewing the performance of the Power department at the State guest house in Rayachoti of Annamayya district on Saturday. Mr. Ravi Kumar instructed the officials to identify areas likely to see a rise in power demand and prepare infrastructure accordingly for the next five years.

The Minister said the government had grounded additional infrastructure works worth around ₹6,200 crore across the State, including transformers, substations and power lines. “More than 200 33/11 KV substations are also being taken up Statewide. Officials should strengthen higher-capacity substations and transmission lines wherever necessary,” he said.

Mr. Ravi Kumar said that officials should expedite works by deploying additional teams wherever required as the government was implementing the ₹700-crore Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) programme. Low-voltage pockets should be identified and distribution transformers upgraded, he said.

The Minister further highlighted that officials should draw up an action plan to ensure daytime quality power supply to farmers and accelerate implementation of PM-KUSUM. “Steps should be taken to prevent power-related accidents, particularly where hazardous lines pass over residential areas,” he said.

Referring to the solar energy projects, the Minister said that 6 lakh connections had already been provided to SC and ST households under the Surya Ghar scheme. He directed officials to expand the programme among the backward-class households, with the State planning an additional assistance of up to ₹20,000 over the Centre’s subsidy towards each connection.

The Minister said that steps were under way to establish an indoor substation at Madanapalle and urged the officials to identify land in advance for future substations.

title: Karnataka teachers can now prefix ‘Tr’ to their names on the lines of ‘Dr’ and ‘Prof’
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
On Teachers’ Day, the Karnataka government has issued an order allowing use of prefix “Tr” before names of teachers, on the lines of “Dr” for doctors and “Prof” for professors.

The order states that the decision is in recognition of teachers’ contribution to “progress and educational upliftment of society.” It highlights multiple contributions of teachers — ranging from career guidance and instilling confidence among students to upholding Constitutional values and building a scientific temper.

Earlier in the day, speaking at the launch of the Praja Seva Department in Kudligi in Vijayanagara district on Saturday, which coincided with Teachers’ Day, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar had called for the new convention of prefixing “Tr” before teachers’ names.

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar waving to people at the public meeting organised to launch the Praja Seva campaign in Kudligi town of Vijayanagara district on Saturday.

Mr. Shivakumar said teachers played an important role in the development of the country as soldiers, workers and farmers do. Their contribution to society, he said, deserved greater recognition and respect, similar to the recognition accorded to professionals such as doctors and professors.

“There are more than 4.5 lakh teachers in Karnataka. A mother who gives us life and a teacher who gives us education are invaluble and deserve special honour,” he said.

The Chief Minister also said that his government was working on an initiative to encourage poor children studying in rural schools with 15% rural reservation, out of which 50% will be reserved for students studying in government rural schools.

title: Uncertainty over tunnel road fuels push for Vilangad-Mananthavady route
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
With the Thamarassery Ghat Road frequently witnessing traffic congestion, the demand for an alternative road connecting Kozhikode and Wayanad is gaining momentum.

The proposed Vilangad-Panom-Kunhome-Mananthavady route is being pushed as a possible alternative, particularly for travellers from north Kozhikode to north Wayanad.

The renewed demand for an alternative route comes amid uncertainty over the Anakkampoyil-Kalladi-Meppadi twin-tube tunnel road project (Kozhikode-Wayanad Tunnel Road). Work on the project was halted after a debris slip near its entrance at Kalladi on July 7, 2026.

The demand for the Vilangad-Mananthavady route is nearly five decades old. The first move to establish a road from Vilangad through Panom to Kunhome, bypassing the ghat, began in 1977. Further efforts were made towards the end of the 1980s and in the early 1990s under the leadership of the MLAs of the time.

The demand gained fresh momentum around 2009, when protests were launched seeking a forest road. A people’s committee organised a march from Vilangad into the forest, but the police stopped the march.

According to residents, only around 3 km of new road needs to be built to connect the existing roads and make the proposed route operational. A wide road already connects Vilangad with Panom, while the distance from Panom to Kunhome is around 7 km. Around 4 km of this stretch is already covered by a coupe road.

Historical significance

Residents said the route had historical significance as it was used in the past by people travelling between Vilangad and Wayanad.

However, the entire 7-km stretch between Panom and Kunhome falls within reserve forest, making forest clearance a major hurdle.

Those who support the project have suggested an elevated road as a possible solution. They said a viaduct could be constructed with minimal disturbance to the forest, allowing wildlife to move underneath it. An earlier study conducted by Vanimel grama panchayat had proposed constructing bridges and culverts as part of the route.

The demand was raised again at a people’s convention held recently to press for the Vilangad-Mananthavady road. The convention was inaugurated by Shafi Parambil, MP.

Committee formed

A committee has been formed to coordinate efforts for the project, with K.M. Abhijith, MLA, as chairman and Kozhikode district panchayat vice-president K.K. Navas as convenor. MPs Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Shafi Parambil and MLA Usha Vijayan have been named chief patrons.

The committee has decided to convene a high-level meeting in Thiruvananthapuram soon. It has also decided to seek funds for a preliminary survey for the proposed route and prepare an expert report for submission to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. Further efforts will be made to seek the Centre’s approval for the project.

Meanwhile, the State government is awaiting an expert panel’s report before deciding whether to resume work on the Anakkampoyil-Kalladi-Meppadi twin-tube tunnel road.
